code_hints: Before any scraping on moncler.com, wait and click cookie acceptance using selectors.modals.cookie_accept (OneTrust). Proceed even if not found.
If a country/region modal appears, click a button/link containing 'United Kingdom' or a generic 'Continue' using selectors.modals.geo_continue.
Do not treat the homepage as PLP. Navigate directly to the seeded PLP start URL from overrides_patch.start_urls.
On PLP, wait for either plp.product_tile or plp.product_link. After content appears, perform incremental scrolls (up to 6) with small delays to trigger lazy loading, then re-query tiles.
Extract PDP URLs from plp.product_link anchors. Normalize them through url_rules before queuing.
On PDP, first try pdp.price [itemprop="price"]; if meta[itemprop="price"] is used, read its content attribute. Also capture pdp.title using the provided fallbacks.
Set the request header Accept-Language to en-GB to reduce geo/locale redirects. If your framework supports it, persist cookies after accepting once to avoid repeated modals.
rationale: We landed on the homepage where no product grid exists and likely encountered cookie/region gates. The safest fix is a configuration-level change: seed a known PLP in the en-GB market, enforce en-gb locale in URLs, and auto-dismiss OneTrust/geo modals. Additional resilient selectors cover typical Moncler/SFCC structures and structured-data fallbacks for price/title on PDP. URL normalization prevents locale traps and accidental hops to monclergroup.com.
